blocking.evidence: policy_probe.py does not implement an always-demote policy. Its demote_all (lines 21-26) calls the module's _demote_once, which already contains the pays test (candidate_selection.py line 254). So 'promote_then_demote' and 'promote_then_pays' are the same policy: policy-probe-result.txt shows identical means (46.557 / 46.557) and 0 wins in both directions, and 'demote_then_promote' is the pays test run before promotion, not always-demote. Only three distinct policies were measured, and the one the document says was beaten (always demote after promotion) was never run. Re-implemented as written (a sharing pair is always converted to its unshared single in place, or removed) and run on the same seed and pool stream, real always-demote-after-promotion scores mean 46.574 against the shipped 46.557 over the same 27,594 comparisons, and wins head-to-head 532 to 305. The document's stated basis for choosing Stage 3 is therefore not what the script measures, and on the script's own metric the shipped test does not have the highest mean.
